I was afraid to tell you this, but I must. There is a man at the university who has written some articles about my thesis work. He is an old friend of my father's, and he has asked me if I would be willing to publish his article as a paper in my thesis. I don't know what to do. It is not that I don't believe him, but I don't understand it either. What does this mean for my thesis? It means that I can't write about anything else. You are right. It might have been better if I hadn't said anything at all. But now I can't stop thinking about it.

You have no reason to fear anything. You will write about what interests you, and it will be fine. If you like, I will help you look up some sources on your own.

Thank you. That would be nice. I have to go. Goodbye.

I lay awake for a long time. The room was cold and I was tired. I fell asleep. I woke up once or twice during the night, but I was too tired to get up again.

When I got up in the morning, the man had gone. I found the girl in the kitchen cooking breakfast. She did not look happy. When she saw me, she gave me a smile that did not reach her eyes.

'Where's the man?' I asked.

'Somebody had to get up early and go to work,' she said. 'He had to leave at six o'clock. But he said he'd be back this evening. He said he was sorry to have to leave, but he's not used to sleeping in strange houses. He didn't sleep well. He told me he would have stayed longer if he'd been able to. But I don't think he'll come back.'

I looked at her. She turned away and started washing up the dishes.

'Is that true?' I asked.

'Of course it's true,' she said. 'Why would I lie? Because I like to hear you say things like that? Because you make me feel good when you talk to me like that?'

'I didn't mean anything like that,' I said.

'Well, maybe you did,' she said. 'But if you did, I wish you hadn't. It makes everything worse.'

I thought about what she had said. I looked around the kitchen. It seemed strange that someone who had only been here one night could have left such an impression behind. I wanted to say something to her. I felt ashamed of what I had done to her the previous evening, but I couldn't find the words to tell her. I couldn't explain why I had been so angry. I could not explain why I had treated her like that. I knew that she was right. I was a fool, and I had acted like a fool. I wanted to tell her that I was sorry. But I couldn't find the words. I could not say the things that were in my heart. I did not know what I should do. I sat down by the fire and looked into the flames.

'You're thinking about the man, aren't you?' she said.

'I don't know who I'm thinking about,' I said.

'That's always been your trouble,' she said. 'You don't know who you are thinking about, or who you're feeling for. You never know what you want. That's why you're always confused. That's what's wrong with you. Do you know what the problem is? It's that you don't know yourself. That's what the problem is. You don't know yourself.'

I looked at her. She was sitting in a chair opposite me. She looked tired. Her eyes were red. I felt sorry for her. I wished I could do something to help her. But I did not know what I should do.

'I wish I did know myself,' I said.

'Well, then, you've got to find out,' she said. 'You've got to try. If you don't try, you'll never find out. If I were you, I'd start by finding out what it was that made you angry. Why did you get so angry yesterday evening? What was it that upset you so much? Maybe it's not just a matter of knowing yourself. Maybe it has something to do with other people too. Maybe you have to find out how other people see you, and how they treat you. Maybe that's part of it too. Maybe that helps you to find out who you are.'

'I wish I knew who I was,' I said.
